Alex —

Thanks for the notes and the diagram. Yes, X-Redwood-Trace-Id is our recommended default and maps cleanly to common tracing systems. A few specifics below and a minimal SDK example.

Observability headers we recommend (defaults):
- X-Redwood-Trace-Id: string (UUID v4 recommended) -> propagated through the request path and included in SDK logs.
- X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: JSON-ish string (url-encoded) with keys: queue_ms, model_ms, network_ms, total_ms. Example: {"queue_ms":12,"model_ms":78,"network_ms":5,"total_ms":95} sent back as header value.
- X-Redwood-Request-Id: short request id for quick lookup in logs (alphanum).

Suggested log fields (structured JSON logs):
- service: "redwood-client"
- trace_id: <X-Redwood-Trace-Id>
- request_id: <X-Redwood-Request-Id>
- model: "redwood/ggml-v2" (example)
- input_tokens, output_tokens
- latency_ms_total, latency_ms_model, latency_ms_queue

Minimal Node snippet (server-side; axios):

const axios = require('axios');
async function callRedwood(prompt, traceId) {
  const res = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', { prompt }, {
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
      'X-Redwood-Trace-Id': traceId || require('crypto').randomUUID(),
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    timeout: 30000
  });
  // parse X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown if present
  const latencyHeader = res.headers['x-redwood-latency-breakdown'];
  return { body: res.data, latencyBreakdown: latencyHeader };
}

Embeddings + reranker pattern: send candidates + query embedding id in the request; response includes per-candidate reranker_score and embedding_id. Example response fragment: 
{ candidates: [{id: 'c1', text: '...', reranker_score: 0.87}, {id: 'c2', text: '...', reranker_score: 0.45}], top_k: 1 }

Retention/telemetry: we retain request-level telemetry (headers + latency) for 90 days for hosted customers by default; for Dedicated/Private we can extend per contract.

I'll paste equivalent Python snippet and a short example for structured output in a follow-up message if helpful.

Alex —

Great — quick answers inline and proposed next steps:

- Serialization: X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown will be a minified JSON string. In HTTP headers it will be URL-encoded by the SDK client automatically; on the server you can url-decode and parse JSON. We'll include an example parser in the SDK snippets.
- Embedding response fields: we return embedding_id as "embedding_id" on each candidate and reranker_score as "reranker_score" (float 0..1). Example: { candidates: [{embedding_id: "vec_123", text: "...", reranker_score: 0.87}, ...] }
- Dashboards: Redwood Console will provide an out-of-the-box Observability dashboard for your account with per-route token usage, p50/p95 latency, error rates, and token-level cost breakdown. We'll also add a custom dashboard widget for any route you want.
- Retention: 90 days by default for hosted accounts, extendable for Dedicated/Private per contract (we captured this on the call).
